Thompson played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]] before being selected by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] as the fourth overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. He won an [[2016 NBA Finals|NBA championship]] with the Cavaliers in 2016 and has also played for the [[Boston Celtics]], [[Sacramento Kings]], [[Indiana Pacers]], [[Chicago Bulls]], and [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Tristan Thompson|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/players/tristan-thompson|website=NBADraft.net|access-date=November 6, 2012}} Thompson also represented [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canada]] in international competitions. ==High school career== Born in [[Brampton]], [[Ontario]], Thompson attended [[St. Marguerite d'Youville Secondary School]] for grades 9 and 10. After making two trips from Brampton to visit a prep school in the [[United States]], Thompson decided to attend [[Saint Benedict's Preparatory School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey]], for his sophomore year, alongside fellow [[University of Texas at Austin]] commit [[Myck Kabongo]]. He cited increased exposure and a higher level of competition as his reasons for transferring.{{cite news | url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/kevin_armstrong/02/26/tristan.thompson/index.html | work=CNN | title=Canadian prospects searching for more exposure at American schools | date=February 27, 2009 | archive-date=November 3, 2012 | access-date=November 25, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103155924/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/kevin_armstrong/02/26/tristan.thompson/index.html | url-status=dead }} Thompson spent his sophomore and half his junior year at St. Benedict's, making an immediate impact and showing flashes of brilliance.{{cite web|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Top-High-School-Prospects-at-the-2007-City-of-Palms-Classic-2421 |title=Top High School Prospects at the 2007 City of Palms Classic |publisher=DraftExpress |access-date=November 6, 2012}} In his short time there, he shot through the ranks to super-stardom, becoming the top recruit in the nation entering his junior season.{{cite web |url=http://www.basketball.ca/en/hm/inside.php?sid=1&id=2336 |title=Canada Basketball |publisher=Basketball.ca |access-date=November 6, 2012 |archive-date=October 1, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111001225951/http://www.basketball.ca/en/hm/inside.php?sid=1&id=2336 |url-status=dead }} The nation's top basketball programs heavily sought Thompson, who made the first verbal commitment of the class of 2010 to [[Rick Barnes]] and the [[Texas Longhorns]].{{cite web|url=http://grassrootsballin.wordpress.com/2008/03/04/tristan-thompson-st-benedicts-nj-class-of-2010-picks-texas |title=Tristan Thompson (St. Benedict's, NJ) Class of 2010 Picks Texas « Grassrootsballin |publisher=Grassrootsballin.wordpress.com |date=March 4, 2008 |access-date=November 6, 2012}} Twenty-one games into his junior year, the relationship between Thompson and then-St. Benedict's coach [[Dan Hurley]] hit a rough patch. Hurley's in-your-face, no-holds-barred coaching style took a toll on the young star. During a game against then-top-ranked [[Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)|Mater Dei]], Hurley confronted Thompson during a time out. A heated debate ensued, and Thompson was sent off the court and later removed from the team.{{cite web|author=Aristide Economopoulos/The Star-Ledger |url=http://blog.nj.com/hssportsextra/2009/02/texas_recruit_tristan_thompson.html |title=Texas recruit Tristan Thompson kicked off St. Benedict's boys basketball team | NJ.com |date=February 12, 2009 |publisher=Blog.nj.com |access-date=November 6, 2012}} Over the next few days he made it known that he was planning to leave, resulting in a barrage of calls from top prep schools throughout North America trying to acquire his services. The next week he transferred to [[Findlay Prep]] with his close friend and [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] teammate [[Cory Joseph]].{{cite web|last=Simmons |first=Steve |url=http://www.torontosun.com/sports/columnists/steve_simmons/2009/02/13/8375606-sun.html |title='Insulting' treatment | Columnists | Opinion |publisher=Toronto Sun |date=February 13, 2009 |access-date=November 6, 2012}}{{cite web|url=http://insidetexas.com/news/story.php?article=838 |title=Tristan Thompson {{sic|nolink=y|Tran|sfering}} to Finlay Prep |publisher=InsideTexas.com |date=November 2, 2012 |access-date=November 6, 2012}} Thompson joined Findlay on the back end of their schedule, making an immediate impact on the team and thriving under Findlay coach Michael Peck's system and coaching style. Thompson solidified his top recruit status and helped lead Findlay to their first national championship. He continued to round and polish his skills in his senior year in preparation for college and held fast to his commitment to the University of Texas, officially signing his letter of intent on November 11, 2009.{{cite web |url=http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111109aaa.html |title=Men's Basketball signs Tristan Thompson to National Letter of Intent – TexasSports.com – Official website of University of Texas Athletics – Texas Longhorns |publisher=TexasSports.com |date=November 11, 2009 |access-date=November 6, 2012 |archive-date=March 5, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120305094447/http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111109aaa.html |url-status=dead }} Thompson then led his team to another National Championship at the ESPN National High School Invitational.{{cite news|title=Findlay Prep Repeats at the Second Annual ESPN RISE National High School Invitational – Corey Joseph MVP|date=April 3, 2010|work=espnmediazone3.com|url=http://www.espnmediazone3.com/us/2010/04/findlay-prep-repeats-at-the-second-annual-espn-rise-national-high-school-invitational-–-corey-joseph-mvp/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101111074400/http://www.espnmediazone3.com/us/2010/04/findlay-prep-repeats-at-the-second-annual-espn-rise-national-high-school-invitational-%E2%80%93-corey-joseph-mvp/|archive-date=November 11, 2010}} After their senior year, Thompson and Joseph both committed to Texas and were the fourth and fifth Canadians to be named [[McDonald's All-American]]s, after [[Bill Wennington]] (1981), [[Barry Bekkedam]] (1986) and [[Olu Famutimi]] (2003).{{cite web |url=http://mcdonaldsallamerican.com/2012/Boy's%20Alumni%20-%202011.xls |title=Every SuperStar Starts with a Nomination |publisher=Mcdonaldsallamerican.com |date=July 22, 2010 |access-date=November 6, 2012 }}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} Thompson was also named a [[Jordan Brand Classic]] All-American.{{cite web |url=http://www.nike.com/jumpman23/classic/2010roster.html |title=Jordan Brand All-American Classic |publisher=Nike.com |access-date=November 6, 2012 |archive-date=July 26, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100726124813/http://www.nike.com/jumpman23/classic/2010roster.html |url-status=dead }} ==College career== Thompson averaged 13.1 points and 7.8 rebounds per game for the Texas Longhorns in 2010–11 as he won the team's Most Valuable Player award, as voted on by his teammates. Nationally, Thompson was one of five finalists for the [[USBWA National Freshman of the Year|Wayman Tisdale Award]], an honour given to the National Freshman of the Year by the U.S. Basketball Writers Association. Thompson won the Big 12 Freshman of the Year honours as well as first-team NABC All-District 8 and USBWA All-District VII honours.{{cite web |url=http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031011aac.html |title=Trio of Longhorns Earn USBWA All-District VII Honors – TexasSports.com – Official website of University of Texas Athletics – Texas Longhorns |publisher=TexasSports.com |date=March 10, 2011 |access-date=November 6, 2012 |archive-date=March 19, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319055632/http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031011aac.html |url-status=dead }} He led the team in rebounding, blocked shots (86), double-doubles (10) and field goal percentage (.546) while ranking second in scoring. He helped Texas conclude the 2010–11 season with a 28–8 record and advanced to the NCAA Tournament Round of 32. The Longhorns finished No. 8 in the final AP poll.{{cite web|url=http://rainmennbl.blogspot.com.au/2012/07/history-and-future-of-basketball-in.html|title=History and Future of Basketball in Canada|work=RainmenNBL.blogspot.com.au|date=July 26, 2011|access-date=July 26, 2012}} Thompson told media after the NCAA tournament that he planned to return to Texas for his sophomore season but changed his mind.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/tournament/2011/news/story?id=6236917|title=Texas' Tristan Thompson to return|publisher=ESPN|date=March 19, 2011|access-date=March 19, 2011}} On April 21, 2011, he declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his last three years of college eligibility.{{cite web|url=http://www.readthehorn.com/sports/4097/report_thompson_will_declare_for_nba_draft|title=Report: Tristan Thompson will declare for NBA draft|work=ReadTheHorn.com|date=April 21, 2011|access-date=April 21, 2011|archive-date=December 13, 2014|archive-url=https://archive.today/20141213152654/http://www.readthehorn.com/sports/4097/report_thompson_will_declare_for_nba_draft|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2011–2020)=== ====2011–12 season: Rookie season==== On June 23, 2011, Thompson was drafted fourth overall in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. At the time, he was the highest drafted Canadian-born player in NBA history,{{cite web|last=Wolstat |first=Ryan |url=http://www.winnipegsun.com/2011/06/23/thompson-makes-canadian-nba-history |title=Thompson makes Canadian NBA history | Basketball | Sports |publisher=Winnipeg Sun |date=June 23, 2011 |access-date=November 6, 2012}} that was until [[Anthony Bennett (basketball)|Anthony Bennett]] and [[Andrew Wiggins]] were selected as the first overall pick in [[2013 NBA draft|2013]] and [[2014 NBA draft|2014]], respectively. Thompson continued to make history, drafted alongside Joseph, who was picked 29th by the [[San Antonio Spurs]], only the second occasion in NBA history to that date that two Canadians were selected in the first round of the same draft, the first being in 1983 when [[Leo Rautins]] and [[Stewart Granger (basketball)|Stewart Granger]] were selected 17th and 25th respectively.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_1983.html |title=1983 NBA Draft |publisher=Basketball-Reference.com |date=June 28, 1983 |access-date=November 6, 2012}} The 2011 draft was also the first time three Texas Longhorn basketball players went in the first round of a draft, when Thompson's former collegiate teammate [[Jordan Hamilton (basketball)|Jordan Hamilton]] went 26th overall to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web |url=http://basketball.ca/en/hm/inside.php?id=5117 |title=Canada Basketball |publisher=Basketball.ca |access-date=November 6, 2012 |archive-date=October 3, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111003040241/http://basketball.ca/en/hm/inside.php?id=5117 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web|author=Kate Hairopoulos |url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/college-sports/headlines/20110624-orange-rush-3-horns-taken-in-nba-draft_s-1st-round-for-first-time.ece |title=Orange rush: 3 Horns taken in NBA draft's 1st round for first time | Dallas-Fort Worth College Sports News – Sports News for Dallas, Texas – SportsDayDFW |publisher=Dallasnews.com |date=June 24, 2011 |access-date=November 6, 2012}} [[File:Tristan Thompson Cavs vs Wizards (cropped).jpg|150px|thumb|right|Thompson during his rookie season in 2012]] During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Thompson attended classes at the University of Texas to finish his college degree.{{cite magazine |author=Tommy Alter |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/basketball/nba/07/28/rookies.lockout/index.html |title=Rookie Tristan Thompson, guard Stephen Curry endure lockout effects – NBA – SI.com |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=July 28, 2011 |access-date=November 6, 2012 |archive-date=December 13, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213225529/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/basketball/nba/07/28/rookies.lockout/index.html |url-status=dead }} Thompson signed his rookie contract with the Cavaliers on December 9, 2011, before the start of training camp.{{cite web|author=Northeast Ohio |url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2011/12/cleveland_cavaliers_sign_irvin.html |title=Cleveland Cavaliers sign Irving, Thompson to rookie deals |publisher=cleveland.com |access-date=November 6, 2012|date=December 9, 2011}} Thompson made his professional debut against his hometown [[Toronto Raptors]] on December 26, 2011. In 17 minutes off the bench, Thompson scored 12 points and pulled in 5 rebounds.{{cite web |last=Wolstat |first=Ryan |url=http://www.torontosun.com/2011/12/26/canadian-thompson-has-strong-nba-debut |title=Canadian Thompson has strong NBA debut | Basketball | Sports |publisher=Toronto Sun |date=December 26, 2011 |access-date=November 6, 2012 |archive-date=April 1, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401040646/http://www.torontosun.com/2011/12/26/canadian-thompson-has-strong-nba-debut |url-status=dead }} Both Thompson and teammate [[Kyrie Irving]] were later named to the 2012 Rising Stars Challenge. However, Thompson was selected to play for Team [[Shaquille O'Neal|Shaq]], while Irving was selected by Team [[Charles Barkley|Chuck]]. Thompson finished the season with averages of 8.2 points and 6.5 rebounds in 60 games as he earned [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] honors, becoming the first Canadian to ever earn All-Rookie team honors in the NBA. ====2012–13 season==== In the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13 season]], Thompson worked on avoiding getting his own shots blocked, and switched his shooting hand from left to right.{{cite news|last=Valade|first=Jodie|title=Tristan Thompson gets advice from an old pro on avoiding blocks: Cleveland Cavaliers Insider|date=November 29, 2012|newspaper=The Plain Dealer|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2012/11/tristan_thompson_gets_advice_f.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130401155003/http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2012/11/tristan_thompson_gets_advice_f.html|archive-date=April 1, 2013|url-status=live}} For most of the season, almost 17%, or one out of six, of his shots were blocked,The league average is 6.3% of shots being blocked. threatening former NBA player [[Danny Fortson]]'s 16.7% rate in [[1997–98 NBA season|1997–98]]. Thompson dropped to around 15% by season's end, which was only reached by three other players before the season.Comparison limited to players who attempted at least 500 field goals in a season since 1997, the earliest for which NBA.com has data.{{cite news|last=Dwyer|first=Kelly|title=Tristan Thompson neared NBA infamy before Zydrunas Ilgauskas taught him how not to get blocked|date=April 17, 2013|work=yahoo.com|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/tristan-thompson-approaching-nba-infamy-zydrunas-ilgauskas-showed-131048180--nba.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130420150631/http://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/tristan-thompson-approaching-nba-infamy-zydrunas-ilgauskas-showed-131048180--nba.html|archive-date=April 20, 2013|url-status=live}} He went on to average 3.7 offensive rebounds per game, which ranked fifth in the NBA and first among second year players, and set the Cavaliers franchise record for most offensive rebounds in a single season with 306 (second in the NBA), surpassing [[Zydrunas Ilgauskas]]' 299 offensive rebounds in the 2004–05 season. He also recorded a team-high 31 double-doubles on the season, becoming just the ninth player in franchise history to total at least 30 double-doubles in a single season. He started all 82 games in 2012–13 as he averaged 11.7 points on .488 shooting, 9.4 rebounds and 0.9 blocks in 31.3 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/tristan_t_thompson/bio/ |title=Tristan Thompson Stats, Video, Bio, Profile |work=NBA.com |access-date=December 13, 2014}} ====2013–14 season==== In the 2013 off-season, Thompson decided to switch his shooting hand to his right instead of his left.{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2013/8/11/4611888/tristan-thompson-shooting-hands-switch|title=Tristan Thompson will switch shooting hands next season|work=SBNation.com|date=August 11, 2013|access-date=October 22, 2013}} Despite the change, he had an almost identical season for the Cavaliers in 2013–14, as he started all 82 games while averaging 11.7 points and 9.2 rebounds in 31.6 minutes per game. He tied for fifth in the Eastern Conference with a team-leading and career-best 36 double-doubles. ====2014–15 season==== During the 2014 off-season, the Cavaliers acquired All-Star forwards [[LeBron James]] and [[Kevin Love]]. Thompson came off the bench for most of the season, providing energy and solidifying his place as one of the best offensive rebounders in the league, averaging 8.5 points and 8 rebounds per game. He played in all 82 games and started 15. The Cavaliers finished with a 53–29 record and made the playoffs for the first time since 2010. Early in the first round, Kevin Love dislocated his shoulder and was ruled out for the rest of the post-season. Thompson became the starter after Love's injury and helped the Cavaliers reach the [[2015 NBA Finals]]. The Cavaliers faced the [[Golden State Warriors]], and lost the series in six games. During the playoffs, Thompson emerged as one of the NBA's best rebounders, especially on the offensive glass. He became a [[restricted free agent (NBA)|restricted free agent]] after the season.{{cite news|last=Davis|first=Scott|title=Tristan Thompson turned down an $80 million contract from the Cavs, and 3 months later it looks like a disaster|date=October 17, 2015|work=Business Insider|via=Yahoo.com|url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/tristan-thompson-turned-down-80-140500082.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151019231950/http://finance.yahoo.com/news/tristan-thompson-turned-down-80-140500082.html|archive-date=October 19, 2015|url-status=live}} ====2015–16 season: Championship season==== On October 22, 2015, Thompson re-signed with the Cavaliers on a five-year, $82 million contract, ending a four-month contract stalemate that caused Thompson to miss training camp, the preseason, and the [[2015 FIBA Americas Championship|FIBA Americas Championship]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/thompson-signing-2015|title=Cavs Re-Sign Forward Tristan Thompson|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2015|access-date=October 22, 2015}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13942794/cleveland-cavaliers-tristan-thompson-agree-5-year-82-million-deal|title=Tristan Thompson re-signs with Cavaliers for 5 years, $82 million|publisher=ESPN|date=October 22, 2015|access-date=October 22, 2015}}{{cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2015/08/10/tristan-thompson-ruled-out-of-canadas-team-at-olympic-qualifier.html|title=Tristan Thompson ruled out of Canada's team at Olympic qualifier|work=[[Toronto Star]]|date=August 10, 2015|access-date=January 23, 2016}} Throughout the 2015–16 season, Thompson shared the starting centre role with [[Timofey Mozgov]]. On January 25, 2016, he recorded a season-high 19 points and 12 rebounds in a 114–107 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160125/MINCLE/gameinfo.html|title=James leads Cavs past Timberwolves for Lue's first|work=NBA.com|date=January 25, 2016|access-date=February 2, 2016}} On March 26, in a win over the New York Knicks, Thompson tied [[Jim Chones]]' franchise record by appearing in his 361st consecutive game for the Cavaliers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160326/CLENYK/gameinfo.html|title=James, Love carry Cavs to 107-93 victory over Knicks|work=NBA.com|date=March 26, 2016|access-date=March 26, 2016}} He broke that record three days later, appearing in his 362nd consecutive game in a loss to the Houston Rockets.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160329/HOUCLE/gameinfo.html|title=Harden, Rockets rally to stuns LeBron-less Cavs, 106-100|work=NBA.com|date=March 29, 2016|access-date=March 29, 2016}} Thompson helped the Cavaliers reach the [[2016 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] for the second consecutive season. There they made NBA history by coming back from a 3–1 deficit against the [[Golden State Warriors]] to win the series in seven games, ending a 52-year championship drought in Cleveland.{{cite news|last=McCauley|first=Janie|title=James and Cavaliers win thrilling NBA Finals Game 7, 93–89|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160619/CLEGSW/gameinfo.html?ls=iref:nbahpt11a|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=June 19, 2016|access-date=October 5, 2017}}{{cite news |last=Ziegler |first=P.J |date=June 19, 2016 |title=Curse broken: Cleveland Cavaliers win NBA Championship |url=http://fox8.com/2016/06/19/547003/ |publisher=[[WJW (TV)|FOX 8 Cleveland]] |access-date=October 5, 2017}} ====2016–17 season==== On December 26, 2016, in a loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]], Thompson became the first player in franchise history to play in 400 consecutive regular-season games.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899906|title=Pistons rout Cavaliers 106-90 while James rests|work=ESPN.com|date=December 26, 2016|access-date=December 27, 2016}} On April 5, 2017, Thompson missed the Cavaliers' game against the [[Boston Celtics]] with a sprained right thumb. Thompson's absence ended his streak of consecutive games played at 447—the longest in team history and the longest active streak in the league at the time.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900547|title=James dominates, Cavs beat Celtics 114-91 in East showdown|work=ESPN.com|date=April 5, 2017|access-date=April 5, 2017}} He missed four games with the injury before returning to action in Cleveland's regular-season finale on April 12 against the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900596|title=Raptors prep for playoffs, beat "resting" Cavaliers 98-83|work=ESPN.com|date=April 12, 2017|access-date=April 13, 2017}} Thompson helped the Cavaliers go 12–1 over the first three rounds of the playoffs to reach the NBA Finals for a third straight season. There the Cavaliers matched-up with the [[Golden State Warriors]], but lost the [[2017 NBA Finals|series]] in five games.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/13/sports/golden-state-warriors-win-nba-championship.html|title=Warriors Win N.B.A. Title, Avenging Themselves Against the Cavaliers|date=June 13, 2017|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=October 5, 2017}}{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2017/jun/12/nba-finals-live-golden-state-warriors-cleveland-cavaliers-game-5|title=NBA finals: Golden State Warriors win title against Cavaliers – as it happened|date=June 13, 2017|work=Guardian|access-date=October 5, 2017}} ====2017–18 season==== On November 2, 2017, Thompson was ruled out for three to four weeks with a left calf strain that he suffered the previous night against the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/status-update-171102|title=Cavaliers Status Update on Tristan Thompson|work=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2017|access-date=November 2, 2017}} On December 12, 2017, he played in his first game since November 1; he went scoreless and did not have a rebound in 6 minutes against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975148|title=James scores 25 has 17 assists, as Cavs beat Hawks 123-114|work=ESPN.com|date=December 12, 2017|access-date=December 12, 2017}} On February 25, 2018, he had a season-high 13 rebounds in 23 minutes in a 110–94 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975640|title=Spurs stop slide, down LeBron, Cavaliers 110-94|work=ESPN.com|date=February 25, 2018|access-date=February 25, 2018}} In Game 7 of the Cavaliers' first-round playoff series against the Pacers, Thompson, who played just 24 minutes in the first six games, made a rare start and had 15 points and 10 rebounds in a 105–101 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401029433|title=7th heaven: LeBron carries Cavaliers past Pacers in Game 7|work=ESPN.com|date=April 29, 2018|access-date=April 29, 2018}} The Cavaliers made it to the [[2018 NBA Finals]], where they were swept by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. ====2018–19 season==== [[File:Tristan Thompson against the Portland Trail Blazers (cropped).jpg|200px|thumb|right|Thompson in January 2019]] To begin the season for the 6–21 Cavaliers, Thompson was averaging career highs in points (12.0) and rebounds (11.6) through 27 games.{{cite web|last=Hill|first=Arthur|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2018/12/tristan-thompson-out-2-to-4-weeks-with-sprained-foot.html|title=Tristan Thompson Out 2-4 Weeks With Sprained Foot|work=HoopsRumors.com|date=December 11, 2018|access-date=December 11, 2018}} However, on December 11, he was ruled out for two to four weeks with a left foot sprain.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/status-update-tristan-thompson-181211|title=Tristan Thompson Status Update|work=NBA.com|date=December 11, 2018|access-date=December 11, 2018}} He returned to action on January 2 against the [[Miami Heat]] after missing 10 games.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071231|title=Richardson leads Wade-less Heat past Cavaliers, 117-92|work=ESPN.com|date=January 2, 2019|access-date=January 3, 2019}} On March 20, against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Thompson returned after missing 26 games with a sore left foot.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071738|title=Sexton's 25 leads Cavs over bruised Bucks missing Giannis|work=ESPN.com|date=March 20, 2019|access-date=March 31, 2019}} ====2019–20 season==== On January 9, 2020, Thompson scored a career-high 35 points with 14 rebounds in a 115–112 overtime win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|title=Cavaliers rally past Pistons, 115-112 in OT|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161205|work=ESPN.com|access-date=January 9, 2020|date=January 9, 2020}} He produced a career-best 12.0 points (51.2% FG), 10.1 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 0.9 blocked shots, and 30.2 minutes in 57 games played (51 starts) with the Cavaliers in [[2019–20 Cleveland Cavaliers season|2019–20]]. He was one of six forwards to average a double-double on at least 50.0% shooting in 2019–20, and the only one of that group to also contribute at least 4.0 offensive boards per contest.{{cite web|title=Celtics Sign Jeff Teague, Tristan Thompson |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-jeff-teague-tristan-thompson|work=nba.com/celtics|access-date=November 30, 2020}} ===Boston Celtics (2020–2021)=== On November 30, 2020, Thompson signed a two-year, $19 million contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web |title=Report: Tristan Thompson signs two-year deal to join Boston Celtics |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2020/11/21/report-tristan-thompson-signs-two-year-deal-to-join-boston-celtics/ |access-date=March 17, 2022 |website=NBC Sports |date=November 21, 2020}} In 54 games for the Celtics in the 2020–21 season, he averaged 7.6 points and 8.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Tristan Thompson 2020-21 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/thomptr01/gamelog/2021/ |website=basketball-reference.com |access-date=February 26, 2025}} ===Sacramento Kings (2021–2022)=== On August 7, 2021, Thompson was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-tristan-thompson|title=Kings Acquire Tristan Thompson|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2021}} He appeared in 30 games for the Kings over the first half of the 2021–22 season, averaging a career high 3-point percentage at 1.000%; as well as 6.2 points and 5.4 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Tristan Thompson 2021-22 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/thomptr01/gamelog/2022/ |website=basketball-reference.com |access-date=February 26, 2025}} ===Indiana Pacers (2022)=== On February 8, 2022, Thompson, [[Tyrese Haliburton]], and [[Buddy Hield]] were traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for [[Justin Holiday]], [[Jeremy Lamb]], [[Domantas Sabonis]], and a 2023 second-round pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-acquire-tyrese-haliburton-buddy-hield-and-tristan-thompson-kings|title=Pacers Acquire Tyrese Haliburton, Buddy Hield, and Tristan Thompson from Kings|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2022}} On February 16, Thompson recorded a season-high 17 points along with 6 rebounds and a block in a win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web|title=Tristan Thompson waived by Pacers after 17-point performance vs Wizards|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/tristan-thompson-waived-indiana-pacers-after-17-point-performance-vs-wizards|access-date=February 17, 2022|website=NBA}} On February 17, after playing four games, the Pacers reached a mutual contract buyout agreement with Thompson.{{Cite web|title=Pacers Waive Tristan Thompson|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-tristan-thompson|access-date=February 17, 2022|website=NBA}} ===Chicago Bulls (2022)=== On February 19, 2022, Thompson signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web|title=BULLS RELEASE MCKINNIE; SIGN THOMPSON|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/draft-bulls-sign-tristan-thompson|access-date=February 19, 2022|website=NBA}} He played in 23 games for the Bulls to finish the 2021–22 season. Thompson spent the 2022–23 season as a free agent after not being re-signed.{{cite news |title=Lakers To Work Out Tristan Thompson, Tony Bradley |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/03/lakers-to-work-out-tristan-thompson-tony-bradley.html |access-date=February 26, 2025 |work=Hoops Rumors |date=March 20, 2023}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2023)=== On April 9, 2023, Thompson signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] ahead of the [[2023 NBA playoffs]],{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Shaquille Harrison and Tristan Thompson|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-shaquille-harrison-and-tristan-thompson-4-9-23|website=NBA.com|date=April 9, 2023|access-date=April 9, 2023}} reuniting with former Cavs teammate [[LeBron James]]. He played in six games for the Lakers during the playoffs, including the May 22, 2023 game where Thompson would [[slam dunk|dunk]] the ball with the assist coming from James in a 113–111 loss in the [[2023 NBA Playoffs|2023 Conference Finals]]. This would be Thompson's last game as a Laker.{{cite web |title=Tristan Thompson 2022-23 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/thomptr01/gamelog/2023/ |website=basketball-reference.com |access-date=February 26, 2025}} ===Return to Cleveland (2023–2025)=== On September 12, 2023, Thompson signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on a one-year contract.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Tristan Thompson|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-tristan-thompson-signing-230912|website=NBA.com|date=September 12, 2023|access-date=September 12, 2023}} On January 23, 2024, he was suspended for 25 games without pay after testing positive for [[ibutamoren]] and [[Ligandrol|SARM LGD-4033]].{{cite web|title=Cavs' Tristan Thompson suspended 25 games without pay by NBA|url=https://www.nba.com/news/tristan-thompson-suspended-25-games|website=NBA.com|date=January 23, 2024|access-date=January 23, 2024}} Thomson would end the season going .608% from the field; a career high. On September 9, 2024, Thompson re-signed with the Cavaliers.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Re-Sign Tristan Thompson|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-tristan-thompson-240909|website=NBA.com|date=September 9, 2024|access-date=September 10, 2024}} In the February 13, 2025 game against the [[Toronto Raptors]], Thompson would come off the bench with four seconds left in the game before proceeding to [[dunk (basketball)|dunk]] the basketball, causing an on-court argument.{{cite web|title=Raptors coach "irked" with Tristan Thompson|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/43820354/raptors-irked-tristan-thompson-late-dunk-cavs-blowout |website=ESPN.com|date=February 13, 2025|access-date=May 22, 2025}} The Cavaliers would go on to win 131–108.{{cite web|access-date=May 22, 2024 |date=February 13, 2025 |title=Raptors vs. Cavs game summery |url=https://www.nba.com/game/cle-vs-tor-0022400774 |website=NBA.com}} Thompson would go on to finish the season averaging 1.7 points per game, 3.4 rebounds per game, and 8.2 minutes per game; all career lows. == Executive career == On August 20, 2026, Thompson joined [[Dubai Basketball]] as a global ambassador.{{Cite web |title=NBA Champion Tristan Thompson joins Dubai Basketball Front Office as Global Ambassador |url=https://dubaibasketball.com/basketball/nba-champion-tristan-thompson-joins-dubai-basketball-front-office-as-global-ambassador/ |access-date=August 20, 2026 |website=Dubai
